newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki rally pauses after four record days.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki rally pauses after four record days.

text.p: Finnish shares eased on Wednesday, breaking a four-day record-breaking trend -- but Nokia supported the overall picture and brokers were unsure if a correction or merely a breather was at hand.

A full technical key reversal point was avoided as the HEX came off its intra-session low, ending down 0.34 percent at 2,689.3 points, brokers said. But the close was below the open which some felt was a negative signal.
"Once shares fall slightly, the buyers disappear," one said. "After the recent spurts, you have to start wondering whether this might not be the beginning of the end," he said.
Some brokers said it was time now to start locking recent gains and limit downside risk with the help of derivatives and that demand for bearish options strategies was picking up.
Nokia closed up 1.00 markka at 303.00, mainly on U.S. high-tech strength carried over from Tuesday but also with a little help from its planned launch of a solar-powered handset.

Forestries corrected recent gains -- the sub-index fell 2.54 percent -- with UPM down 2.50 markka at 100.00, Enso down 1.50 at 39.00 and Metsa-Serla down 1.00 at 37.00 after a report that Norscan pulp inventories were largely unchanged in December.

Finland's largest bank Merita see-sawed and eventually trimmed its recent strong gains, down 0.30 at 16.00 in lively dealings. However, its B share with preferential dividend rights added 0.20 to 17.20.
